title: Reasonable and Prudent Parent Standard
statement: The standard covers everyday activities. It does not let you go against a law, a rule, or a court order. Ask your social worker what needs approval first, like travel out of state.
source_name: 22 CCR 89377(b); CDSS RPPS Resource Guide p. 3; WIC 362.05; SOC 156
source_says: Applying the reasonable and prudent parent standard shall not result in denying the rights of a "child" ... or contradict court orders
steps: Ran a SELECT on rights_duties for this id and field; the after text is in the live row. First two sentences check out: WIC 362.05(a)(1) covers 'age-appropriate extracurricular, enrichment, and social activities'; 22 CCR 89377(b) bars contradicting court orders; the CDSS RPPS Resource Guide (ccld.dss.ca.gov/res/pdf/RPPS_ResourceGuide.pdf) p. 3 says the standard does not allow decisions 'that conflict with applicable statute or regulation'. The example 'like travel out of state' has no source: WIC 362.05, 22 CCR 89377, the RPPS guide, the CDSS RPPS page and form SOC 156 (12/11) say nothing about out-of-state travel needing approval. SOC 156 item 16 only requires notice of a foster parent absence of 48 hours or longer. Two searches of cdss.ca.gov and courts.ca.gov found no statewide rule.
fix: The standard covers everyday activities. It does not let you go against a law, a rule, or a court order. If you are not sure whether something needs approval first, ask your social worker.

title: Follow Reasonable Rules
statement: Your caregiver can set fair house rules. Rules cannot take away your rights.
source_name: 22 CCR 89372(a)(5)(B), (b)(1); Foster Youth Rights Handbook pp. 16-18
source_says: Restrict the telephone use of the "child" as reasonable discipline except as provided in (D) below
steps: Ran a SELECT on rights_duties for this id and field; the after text is in the live row. First sentence holds: 22 CCR 89372(b)(1) on Justia says caregivers are not prohibited 'from establishing house rules for the protection of a "child" or household members'. Second sentence is too absolute. 89372(a)(5)(B) lets a caregiver restrict phone use as reasonable discipline and 'Restrict Internet usage when appropriate.' The Ombudsperson handbook p. 16 says 'Your caregiver can temporarily take away your right to make or get some phone calls as a consequence.' Calls to lawyers, social workers and CASA cannot be restricted (89372(a)(5)(D)). WIC 16001.9 has no words about house rules.
fix: Your caregiver can set fair house rules. House rules cannot take away most of your rights. Your caregiver can put fair limits on a few things, like phone and internet use. No one can stop you from calling your lawyer, your social worker, or the Ombudsperson.

title: Follow Reasonable Rules

WIC 16001.9 on Justia does list the rights, but a term check of the section found no mention of house rules or rules of the home. 22 CCR 89372 allows house rules and lets a caregiver 'Restrict the telephone use of the "child" as reasonable discipline' and 'Restrict Internet usage when appropriate', so the flat statement that rules cannot take rights away leaves out those limits.

title: Right to File a Grievance
statement: If the county treats you unfairly, you can send a complaint to the Director of your county child welfare agency. Ask the county how its grievance process works and what it covers.
source_name: CDSS Manual of Policies and Procedures 31-020
source_says: Grievance procedures shall be developed to review complaints from foster parents, legal parents, guardians, and children concerning the placement or removal of a child from a foster home.
steps: Ran a SELECT on rights_duties for this id and field; the after text is in the live row. The CDSS-hosted cws1.pdf was blocked (robots), so read two hosted copies of the same manual (the URL given and advokids.org/wp-content/uploads/pdf/DSS-Manual-Abridged.pdf); they match. 31-020 covers only complaints about placing a child or removing a child from a foster home, not unfair treatment in general. The request is filed with 'the county', not sent to the Director: .34 'The complainant shall file the review request within ten calendar days after becoming aware of the action under complaint.' .61: 'the county director shall issue a final written decision'. .2 lists removals that get no review. The Judicial Council booklet has nothing on complaints.
fix: If you disagree with where the county placed your child, or with the county moving your child out of a foster home, you can file a written grievance with the county. You must file it within 10 days of learning about it. Some moves are not covered. The county director makes the final decision. For other problems, ask the county how to file a complaint and tell your lawyer.

statement: If a referee decided something in your case, and the referee was not sitting as a temporary judge, you can ask a judge to hear it again. The judge can say yes or no.
source_says: A rehearing must be granted if proceedings before the referee were not recorded by an official court reporter or other authorized reporting procedure.
steps: Ran a SELECT on rights_duties for this id and field; the after text is in the live row. Searched 'WIC 252 rehearing referee', Justia WIC 252 failed to load, opened rule 5.542 on courts.ca.gov. (a) confirms the first sentence ('a referee not acting as a temporary judge'). 'The judge can say yes or no' is true only if the hearing was recorded: (c) 'the judge ... may, after reading the transcript of the proceedings, grant or deny'. Under (b) the judge must grant it if there was no record, and under (c) it is deemed granted if not denied within 20 calendar days.
fix: If a referee decided something in your case, and the referee was not sitting as a temporary judge, you can ask a judge to hear it again. If a court reporter recorded the hearing, the judge can say yes or no. If no one recorded it, the judge must say yes.

title: Right to Ask a Judge to Rehear a Referee's Decision
statement: If a referee who was not sitting as a temporary judge decided, you can ask a judge to look again. You only have 10 days after you get the written order.
source_says: may be made by the child, parent, or guardian at any time before the expiration of 10 calendar days after service of a copy of the order and findings.
steps: Ran a SELECT on rights_duties for this id and field; the after text is in the live row. Read rule 5.542(a) on courts.ca.gov. Rule 5.540(c) says the same 10 calendar days.

title: Visit Your Child Consistently
statement: WIC §362.1: visits should be as frequent as possible. WIC §366.21: at review hearings the court looks at whether you visited your child regularly.
source_says: Visitation shall be as frequent as possible, consistent with the well-being of the child.
steps: Ran a SELECT on rights_duties for this id and field; the after text is in the live row. Searched 'WIC 362.1 visitation', opened FindLaw. The entry drops 'consistent with the well-being of the child'; (a)(1)(B) adds 'No visitation order shall jeopardize the safety of the child.' The 366.21 half checks out: opened WIC 366.21 on FindLaw, (g)(1)(A) 'consistently and regularly contacted and visited with the child' and (e)(5) 'the parent has failed to contact and visit the child'.
fix: WIC §362.1: visits should be as frequent as possible, as long as that is good for your child. WIC §366.21: at review hearings the court looks at whether you visited your child regularly.

title: Right to a Hearing Before Placement Gets Stricter
statement: The county must file a petition and there must be a hearing before a judge orders a stricter placement. In an emergency, your child can be moved first and the hearing comes soon after.
source_says: shall be made only after noticed hearing upon a supplemental petition.
steps: Ran a SELECT on rights_duties for this id and field; the after text is in the live row. Searched 'WIC 387 supplemental petition', opened FindLaw. (b): 'The supplemental petition shall be filed by the social worker'. (e): detention pending the petition 'may be made only after a hearing'. Opened WIC 306 on public.law: a social worker may take 'a child who has been declared a dependent child' into temporary custody without a warrant in immediate danger. Opened WIC 315: hearing 'not later than the expiration of the next judicial day' after the petition is filed.
